data.body: Gate held by an inherited failure, not mine. On my branch (stacked on github/mrq-108-review-depth @ 1318094) the hermetic suite runs 39.4s — UNDER the 45s budget — and 559/559 tests pass except tests/node/mrq-99-organizer-copy.test.mjs, which asserts ReviewerPage.tsx contains 'Scorecard (optional)'. That string is present on github/main and absent from MRQ-108's ReviewerPage rewrite, so the parent branch is red on its own. MRQ-108's delegator notified (surface:417). Holding at in_validation; will rebase --onto their fixed tip and re-run pr-gate. My own surfaces are validated end-to-end against the running app (see the attached validation artifact + screenshots).

Second inherited red from the parent: tests/node/bulk-paths.AC-66-69.test.mjs has no census entry for review.routes.ts::reviewsForSubmissions, added by MRQ-108's e60d6fb. Not mine to classify — my new modules (evaluation-results.routes.ts, review-aggregate.ts) contain zero dynamic placeholder expansions. MRQ-108 notified. Suite timing across runs tonight: 39.4s at load 68, 63.6s at load 42 — the budget signal is contention noise, not a code regression; will report the run I gate on.

PR #81 open: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/81 — stacked on MRQ-108, merge that first.

LOCAL GATE (green):
{ "command": "pr-gate", "ticket": "MRQ-109", "status": "pass", "elapsedMs": 63804, "budgetMs": 120000 }
Suite hermetic and under its own budget in the passing run; 1-min load 33 at gate time.

Deviations/flags for the orchestrator:
1. Spawned code-review unavailable — lattice's auto-fired reviewer exited 1 with 'You've hit your session limit · resets 6am (America/New_York)'. Self-reviewed per COMMON.md fallback; the artifact is attached and it caught two real honesty defects in my own diff (MAX->MIN weighting basis; 'No reviews' -> 'Not scored').
2. Two inherited reds from the parent branch cost about 25 minutes: the MRQ-99 copy contract and the bulk-path census entry for reviewsForSubmissions. Both were MRQ-108's and both are now fixed on their tip; re-stacked with --onto each time they rewrote history.
3. No AC IDs minted (not mine to mint) — new tests carry the CONTRACT title prefix with the rubric id in the title text.
4. Scope note: I did not add a 'has reviews' status filter or seed scored evaluations. The seed writes score=null/criteria_scores=null for all 60 evaluations, so the demo results table is a column of dashes until a reviewer scores something. Worth a follow-up ticket if the eval run wants a populated results table on arrival — it is seed policy, not this ticket's.

Merge-captain queue: holding, not pushed. The rebase onto main b526d5d was already finished locally before the stand-by order arrived — sole conflict was cli/api-registry.json, regenerated per the rule (136 ops). Local branch a76dc55 sits 18 commits ahead of main (my 7 plus MRQ-108's, which has not merged, so the stack is intact). Nothing force-pushed; PR #81 still shows the pre-rebase tip. The rebase is one conflict resolution plus a registry regen, so re-doing it on my turn against a newer main costs almost nothing.

Gate on the rebased tree: every check PASSES — worker/client/test types, production build, shell truth, design contract, API contract, hermetic suite (status pass-over-budget), AC trace. The only failure is the gate's own 120s wall-clock: 195s and 201s across two runs, with the suite alone 172s at 1-min load 98. Same branch ran 39.4s and 63.8s earlier tonight.

check:speed (not a gate step) flags submissions-filter-sort p95 over budget. I A/B'd it because my aggregate touches that exact query: with my three correlated subqueries REVERTED the numbers got WORSE — filter-sort 1639ms vs 248ms with them, and two unrelated client metrics (submissions-first-interactive 1490 vs 1000, admin-route-transition 1169 vs 300) blew their budgets in the same run. admin-route-transition does not touch my SQL at all. These are contention measurements, not a regression from this diff.

Merged main (dd18440) into mrq-109-chair-results per the merge captain — merge commit 133859e, pushed. Not rebased.

GATE GREEN:
{ "command": "pr-gate", "ticket": "MRQ-109", "status": "pass", "elapsedMs": 32370, "budgetMs": 120000 }
Hermetic suite: 96 files, 638/638 tests, 28.2s against the 45s objective, at 1-min load 9. No flake seen — the MRQ-90 rate-limit test passed first try. This also settles last night's timing question: identical code ran 172s at load 98 and 28s at load 9, so the earlier over-budget readings were contention, exactly as suspected.

CONFLICT RESOLUTIONS (3):
1. cli/api-registry.json — generated. Took a side, rebuilt the worker, regenerated: 144 operations. Never hand-edited.
2. tests/integration/apply-migrations.ts — union, both kept: 0009_file_comments (main) AND 0009_criterion_kinds (MRQ-108), import and splitStatements lines in matching order. Not renumbered; D1 tracks by filename.
3. src/ui/evaluation/EvaluationPage.tsx — REAL CODE, reconciled by reading both sides. Main's MRQ-107 added reviewer-invite state, an 'Invite reviewer' header button, and an invite footer button; my side replaced the committee row's broken progress ratio with the per-reviewer roll-up. Kept ALL of MRQ-107's invite affordances and dropped none of them, and re-applied my roll-up onto their version of the row. Deleted nothing of theirs.

VALIDATED POST-MERGE against the running app, because that resolution was hand-written: 'Invite reviewer' button present, invite footer present, progress rows read 20/20 reviewed at a fixed 104px, 'View results' and 'Export scores' present, results table sorts 4.15/3.50*/2.80 -> 2.80/3.50*/4.15 with the header box stable at 104px both ways, and the CSV downloads. Screenshot attached.

STANDING FLAG for the Merge Warden: MRQ-108 is still NOT on main, and this branch carries its commits (it was cut from that branch). Squash-merging #81 therefore lands MRQ-108's review-depth work too. My own code was deliberately built to not depend on it, so I can unstack onto main if you would rather land them separately — say the word. Not doing it unasked, since merge order is yours.

Merged main (e3cfce6, the PR #91 untracking) into mrq-109-chair-results — merge commit 8aff08e, pushed. Not rebased.

ONE conflict this time, the expected modify/delete on cli/api-registry.json. Resolved as 'git rm -f cli/api-registry.json' — accepted main's deletion, did NOT regenerate it into the commit, did not re-add it to .gitignore (already there at line 19). The regenerated copy my previous merge commit (133859e) carried is now gone from the branch; 'git ls-files cli/' shows only the six .mjs sources. Working tree clean, so the build's local regeneration is correctly ignored.

GATE PASS:
- worker/client/test types, production build, shell truth, design contract, API contract (cliRegistry: checked — it still passes with the file untracked), route map, AC trace: all pass.
- Hermetic suite: 96 files, 638/638 tests. 66.3s, over its own 45s objective, at 1-min load 35 — status pass-over-budget, and the gate's 120s budget was met, so pr-gate is green overall. Same branch, same code, ran 28.2s at load 9 forty minutes ago; the suite content did not change between those runs.

No re-validation needed for this merge: the only change since the browser pass I attached earlier is the removal of a generated artifact that ships in no runtime path.

Standing flag unchanged: MRQ-108 is still not on main and this branch carries its commits, so squash-merging #81 lands its review-depth work too. Happy to unstack onto main if you would rather land them separately — your call.

PR #81 MERGED (main 7c064bd). The auto-merge fired while I was mid-rebase, so my unstack never landed and was ultimately unnecessary — my force-push was rejected with 'stale info' because the branch was already gone.

VERIFIED MAIN AFTER THE MERGE, because my branch carried MRQ-108's commits at snapshot c832568 while their branch had moved on to eff3bce — a squash of a stale copy could have reverted their later fixes. It did not:
- My work present: src/lib/review-aggregate.ts, src/routes/evaluation-results.routes.ts, score_asc in the sort registry.
- MRQ-108's late fixes present: reviewsForSubmissions in the bulk-path census, completed_truncated in ReviewerPage.
- MRQ-107's invite affordances and my per-reviewer roll-up coexist in EvaluationPage (openInvite x4, reviewerProgress x2) — the hand-merged block survived.
- Full gate on main 7c064bd: PASS. 97 files, 641/641 tests. Suite 89.7s over its 45s objective at load 21, gate 97.5s inside its 120s budget.
- MRQ-108 had in fact already merged as ebd697c (#79, 14:38); my earlier --grep missed it because the squash title reads 'MRQ-108: Review depth...'. So the standing flag I carried about #81 smuggling its work is moot — by merge time that content was already on main.

FLEET FOOTGUN worth broadcasting: after #91 untracked cli/api-registry.json, any worktree that regenerated it before the untracking still has the stale file on disk, and check:api then fails with cli-registry-hash-mismatch against CURRENT MAIN. It reads exactly like a broken main and is not — 'rm -f cli/api-registry.json' clears it. I hit this verifying main and lost a gate run to it; every agent who ran the old regenerate instruction has one.

Board reconciliation 2026-08-12: verified DONE. PR #81 (mrq-109-chair-results) merged 2026-08-12T14:41:03Z; merge commit 7c064bd1 confirmed an ancestor of github/main via 'git merge-base --is-ancestor'. Ticket had drifted at pr_open. The repo has zero open and zero closed-unmerged PRs, so nothing is waiting on review. Status corrected to reflect merge, not PR-open.
